items.title: Trump won't rule out ground troops in Iran as strikes enter third day

featured_image.name: Donald Trump won't rule out boots on ground in Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday declined to rule out deploying American ground forces to Iran, telling the New York Post he would send them "if necessary" as U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran continued into their third day under Operation Epic Fury.[1]

"I don't have the yips with respect to boots on the ground — like every president says, 'There will be no boots on the ground.' I don't say it," Trump told the Post. "I say 'probably don't need them,' [or] 'if they were necessary.'"[2][1]

At the Pentagon, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth struck a similar tone during the first detailed briefing since the operation began on Saturday, refusing to specify what the administration would or would not do. "President Trump ensures that our enemies understand we'll go as far as we need to go to advance American interests," Hegseth said, appearing alongside Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine.[3][4]

items.title: Six US troops killed as Trump won't rule out ground forces in Iran

featured_image.name: War in the Mideast widens as Trump says strikes on Iran ...

items.description:
The United States is "not currently postured" to send ground forces into Iran, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Monday, even as President Donald Trump refused to take the option off the table and the American military campaign entered its third day with mounting casualties on both sides.[1][2]

Rubio, speaking on Capitol Hill before briefing the congressional "Gang of Eight," said the administration is confident its objectives can be achieved through air and naval power alone. But in comments to the New York Post, Trump struck a different tone: "Probably don't need them," he said of ground troops, adding, "if they were necessary" — a stark departure from the traditional presidential assurance of "no boots on the ground."[3][4]

items.title: Saudi Arabia goes on full military alert after Iranian drone strikes

featured_image.name: Return to Your Senses': Gulf States Ramp Up Iran Criticism ...

items.description:
Saudi Arabia raised its military readiness to "full alert" on Monday after Iranian drones struck the massive Ras Tanura refinery on the kingdom's Gulf coast, as the Gulf Cooperation Council condemned Tehran's attacks across six member states and warned it reserves the right to retaliate.[1][2]

The escalation came three days into a widening Middle East conflict that began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched airstrikes against Iran. Tehran responded with volleys of missiles and drones targeting GCC nations that host American military installations, killing at least six people and injuring more than 100 across the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and Saudi Arabia.[3][2]

items.title: Ukraine says it recaptured more land than Russia seized in February

featured_image.name: Ukraine's military makes gains in southeast region of ...

items.description:
Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced on March 2 that Ukrainian defense forces reclaimed more territory in February than Russian troops managed to seize — the first time Kyiv has outpaced Moscow in territorial gains since the Kursk Oblast incursion into Russian territory in the summer of 2024.[1][2]

"In February 2026, for the first time since the Kursk offensive operation, the Ukrainian defence forces regained control of more territory than the enemy managed to capture," Syrskyi wrote on Telegram. "We have survived this difficult battle for winter."[2][1]

items.title: Rubio says Israel's strike plan triggered US attack on Iran

featured_image.name: US says Rubio to visit Israel on Monday to discuss Iran ...

items.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio disclosed Monday that the United States launched its attack on Iran after learning that Israel was determined to strike with or without American participation, a revelation that cast the joint military operation in a new light and raised fresh questions about the administration's legal justification for war.

"We knew that there was going to be an Israeli action. We knew that that would precipitate an attack against American forces, and we knew that if we didn't preemptively go after them before they launched those attacks, we would suffer higher casualties," Rubio told reporters on Capitol Hill before briefing congressional leaders.[1][2]

items.title: Trump refuses to rule out ground troops in Iran

featured_image.name: What is Trump's approval rating? Iran strikes controversial in polls

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Monday he would not rule out sending American ground troops into Iran, declaring that Operation Epic Fury is progressing faster than expected as the U.S. military campaign entered its third day with mounting casualties on both sides.

"I don't have the yips with respect to boots on the ground — like every president says, 'There will be no boots on the ground.' I don't say it," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published March 2. "I say 'probably don't need them,' or 'if they were necessary.'"[1][2]
